issues.legal_issue: The statutory trade-control scheme and a notification issued under it do not extend to forest produce grown on government land, so they do not rescind contracts concerning that produce.
material_facts: The existing contracts concerned the collection, purchase, and removal of sal seeds grown in government forests.

The legislation’s stated purpose was to prevent smuggling of forest produce grown both on private holdings and government land by making the government the exclusive purchaser of produce grown on private holdings; the statement of purpose distinguished sal seeds as grown only in government forests.
The scheme’s provisions concerning appointed agents, purchasing, depots, prices, registration, and sale dealt with the government’s purchase of produce from private holdings.
The government issued a notification bringing the legislation into force for sal seeds and then treated the existing contracts as rescinded.
The appeals challenged the dismissal of petitions seeking a declaration that the notification had not rescinded the contracts.
issues.conclusion: The legislation and the notification do not apply to forest produce grown in government forests; the government could not treat the contracts concerning that produce as rescinded.
issues.legal_principle: A statute must be interpreted as a whole, in light of its purpose, preamble, scheme, and context; general words may be given a restricted meaning where their literal breadth would conflict with the statute’s object and scheme. Sections 1(3), 2, 4, 5(1), 5(3), and 7–12 of the Orissa Forest Produce (Control of Trade) Act, 1981, read together, show a scheme for government purchase of forest produce grown on private holdings. The Court relied on Attorney General v. H.R.H. Prince Augustus, [1957] 1 All ER 49; Chertsey, U.D.C. v. Mixnam’s Properties, [1964] 2 All ER 627; Empress Mills v. Municipal Committee, Wardha, AIR 1958 SC 341; and Maunsell v. Olins, [1975] 1 All ER 16. It was unnecessary to decide whether Explanation II to section 5(1) independently saved the contracts.

rule.if: government_forest_produce and scheme_centers_on_purchase_from_private_growers and notification_targets_that_produce and appeal_challenges_contract_rescission

predicates.government_forest_produce: The contract concerns forest produce grown on land owned by the government.
predicates.scheme_centers_on_purchase_from_private_: The statutory scheme provides for the government to purchase forest produce from private growers, rather than to purchase produce grown on its own land.
predicates.notification_targets_that_produce: The government issues a notification applying the trade-control scheme to the kind of produce covered by the contract.
predicates.appeal_challenges_contract_rescission: An appeal challenges a ruling that a government notification rescinded an existing contract concerning forest produce.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a contract for produce grown on government land and the statutory scheme centers on government purchase from private growers, a notification applying that scheme to the produce does not rescind the contract.

issues.legal_issue: A court hearing an appeal cannot extend a lease to compensate for the period during which the lessee was unable to collect produce, but may leave the parties to work out their rights in light of the declaration and interim orders.
material_facts: The government treated the contracts as rescinded, and the appellants were unable to collect and purchase produce for a period of the lease.
The appellants asked the Court to extend the lease to make up for that lost period.
Interim orders had been made during the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to extend the lease and left the parties to work out their rights in light of the declaration and the interim orders.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that it was not permissible to extend the lease by way of relief for the business lost; the parties were left to work out their rights after taking account of the interim orders and the declaration granted.

predicates.appeal_seeks_lease_extension: In an appeal, a party asks the court to extend a lease to compensate for time lost during the dispute.
predicates.collection_period_lost: The party was unable to collect the contracted produce for part of the lease term because the other contracting party treated the contract as ended.
predicates.interim_orders_made: The court made interim orders during the proceedings.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks an extension for a lost collection period and interim orders were made, the lease is not extended and the parties work out their rights in light of the orders.
